name: Mandibular development softmaxxing

lead: Mandibular development softmaxxing refers to non-surgical efforts to improve the lower jaw: a more defined jawline, forward growth, or better lower-face proportions. It sits in the 'softmaxx' side of looksmaxxing, as opposed to surgery.

The best-known related practice is mewing, which emphasizes resting tongue posture. The American Association of Orthodontists reports no evidence that mewing improves the jaw, according to Wikipedia; no trial has tested a combined mandibular routine.

paras: Practitioners typically combine oral posture habits (tongue against the palate, lips closed), chewing tougher foods, and leanness or neck training to make the jawline look sharper. Results are usually assessed by comparing photos over months.

Posture habits are generally low-risk. Over-chewing or hard gum can cause jaw muscle or joint discomfort, and orthodontists note that unproven devices should not replace treatment of real jaw problems.

chain: Claimed influence on jaw muscle tone and growth
angle.text: Practitioners use posture and chewing routines hoping for a more defined jaw. Visible change in practice can also come from reduced facial fat and photo conditions.

lead: Mandibular development softmaxxing is the community term for non-surgical attempts to enhance the lower jaw. Participants aim for a more prominent or defined mandible and chin, which many looksmaxxing guides associate with a stronger-looking face.

The practice overlaps with mewing, an oral posture technique named after British orthodontist John Mew and promoted by his son Mike Mew. Wikipedia describes mewing as unproven, reports that interest rose from 2019 through social media and looksmaxxing communities, and says the American Association of Orthodontists reports no evidence it improves the jaw.[1]

Because the look of a jawline also depends on body fat and neck and chin soft tissue, some participants pair these routines with leaning out. No study has specifically tested a mandibular softmaxxing routine.

paras: The term groups together routines described as 'soft' because they do not involve surgery. Common components are tongue posture, chewing, and general lean-physique work for a sharper jawline.[1]

Mewing, the best-known associated method, asks practitioners to rest the tongue against the roof of the mouth. It derives from orthotropics, developed by John Mew.[1] Wikipedia reports that Mike Mew was removed from the UK dental register in 2024 following a misconduct process, and that most orthodontists do not regard mewing as a substitute for jaw surgery.[1]

timeline.event: Interest in mewing rises sharply through social media and looksmaxxing communities.[1]
Mike Mew is removed from the UK dental register.[1]
